course_description:
Expansion on theoretical and practical knowledge of basic sport and exercise psychology. Emphasis on theoretical basis of applied sport and exercise psychology and the development of practical skills that can be employed as teachers, coaches, fitness professionals and exercise scientists.

This course adopts a solution-focused and case-based learning approach to applied sport and exercise psychology. Each week, students will engage with real-world performance psychology cases designed to mirror the challenges and opportunities practitioners encounter in elite sport, the performing arts, and other high-pressure domains. Grounded in the Creative Problem-Solving (CPS) framework, students will work in small groups to address weekly cases by progressing through key phases of the model: problem definition, information gathering, idea generation, evaluation, implementation, and adaptation. Each phase is supported by short, targeted lectures that develop relevant theoretical and applied knowledge. Students will also critically evaluate competing evidence, developing the skills to build strong, evidence-informed arguments to justify their proposed interventions. This integrated format fosters teamwork, critical thinking, and practitioner confidence.

The course is divided into three sections:

Section 1: Problem Solving (Weeks 2–6)

Because performers, teams, and organisations often seek performance psychology support when facing a challenge, it is important to develop strong problem-solving capabilities. The first section of the course focuses on common issues encountered in applied practice and explores evidence-informed strategies to address them.

Section 2: Preparation (Weeks 7–8)

Once an intervention has been identified, practitioners must prepare performers to implement it effectively. This section focuses on performance preparation, with students applying psychological strategies to optimise their own performance for the Week 8 oral presentation. By experiencing these strategies first-hand, students will gain a deeper appreciation of their practical application and effectiveness.

Section 3: Optimisation (Weeks 9–13)

Beyond solving problems, performers, teams, and organisations are often proactive in seeking support before challenges arise. The final section of the course focuses on performance psychology strategies designed to optimise performance, adaptability, wellbeing, and long-term development.

course_aims: This course will expand upon the theoretical and practical knowledge base of PSYC2000. Classical and contemporary topics within sport and exercise psychology will be studied, with a particular focus on successfully navigating the field of elite sport and performance as an applied practitioner.

learning_outcomes.description: further understand the influence that participation in sport or exercise have upon individuals' psychological development.
further understand the role that social psychological variables play in participation and performance in sport and exercise.
understand the theoretical basis of applied sport psychology
develop practical skills and applied psychological techniques that you can employ as teachers, coaches, fitness professionals, or athletes.
understand the basic interventions commonly used by sport psychologists
understand the role that culture can play within sport psychology.
work effectively within a team in order to develop communication and process management skills, and facilitate peer-assisted, collaborative learning.

assessment_details.task_description: Working in small teams, students analyse a real or realistic performance-related challenge (e.g., sport, performing arts, military, healthcare, education) from the perspective of an applied sport and exercise psychology practitioner. Using one psychological theoretical framework, students develop an evidence-informed intervention by analysing the challenge, generating and evaluating potential solutions, and recommending an appropriate course of action. The assessment consists of a concise written practitioner brief (2 pages) summarising the team's analysis and proposed intervention, and an 8-minute group presentation (plus 2 minutes of questions) where students present and justify their recommendations to a simulated client or organisation. The assessment develops students' ability to apply psychological theory to practice, critically evaluate evidence, collaborate effectively, and communicate professional recommendations. assessment_details.title: Structured Team Debate
assessment_details.task_description: In teams, students participate in a structured debate exploring a contemporary issue in sport and exercise psychology. Each team selects (or proposes) a debate question, adopts a position, and constructs an evidence-informed argument supported by psychological theory and research. During the debate, teams present their position, critically question an opposing team, defend their arguments, and respond to challenging questions in real time. The assessment includes a short reference list (minimum 10 academic sources) submitted prior to the debate and an in-class debate consisting of an opening position statement, questioning and defence, and a closing statement. The assessment develops students' critical thinking, evidence-based reasoning, oral communication, and ability to engage in professional discussion while applying psychological theory to complex and often contested issues in sport and exercise psychology. learning_activities.topic: Week 1: Introduction + Performance Theories and Frameworks Because this course focuses on performance, it is important to start by defining what performance is and how performance psychology relates to it. This session will explore the difference between a clutch performer and a choke artist, introduce the concept of flow state, and present the Individual Zone of Optimal Functioning (IZOF) model. The Gold Medal Profile will also be introduced as a foundational framework for this course. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05, L06

Week 2: Lack of motivation After many years of repeating the same routines to master their craft, performers may experience a lack of motivation. While solutions are often “person-oriented”, this class will examine person–environment interactions that can impact motivation in order to identify more holistic solutions to this problem. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05, L06

Week 3: Performance Anxiety As a performer improves, they are increasingly exposed to high-stakes situations (e.g., international competitions, Olympics and Paralympics team selection), which can provoke anxiety that may impair performance. This class will explore various methods for managing anxiety, ranging from cognitive behavioural strategies to mindfulness-based approaches. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05, L06

Week 4: Team dysfunction In team sports, problems are often not located within individuals but rather between them. Building on various team functioning frameworks, this class will analyse a case of team dysfunction to better understand the psychological and interpersonal processes required to enhance team dynamics and cohesion. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05, L06

Week 5: Choking, Lost Move Syndrome, and Yips Even when performers have mastered their craft in training, some struggle to perform at the same level in competition. This phenomenon, often referred to as “choking,” has been widely studied, and several strategies have been tested to mitigate it. This class will examine these strategies to help performers deliver their best when it matters most. While less common than choking, some athletes may completely lose the ability to perform a movement they once executed with ease. This issue — known as Lost Move Syndrome or the yips — has also been studied and will be discussed in this class. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05, L06

Week 6: Coping with adversity (e.g., de-selection, injuries) High performance sport inevitably comes with significant challenges. Athletes must therefore develop the capacity to cope with adversity. Drawing on resilience frameworks, this class will use two cases, de-selection and injury, to explore how mental skills can be used to support performers through difficult times. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05, L06

Week 7: Pre-Performance Routine To enhance consistency, enter optimal psychological states, and manage distractions, performers can benefit from developing a Pre-Performance Routine (PPR). This class will examine evidence-based models of PPRs and the distinction between routines and superstitions. Students will then apply these principles by designing and implementing their own pre-performance routine in preparation for their Week 8 group oral presentation, providing an opportunity to experience these strategies firsthand and reflect on their effectiveness. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05, L06
Week 8: Group oral presentation (Assessment task) See assessment for details Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05, L06, L07

Week 9: Mental health Mental health and wellbeing are increasingly recognised and discussed in today’s society, and high-performance sport is no exception. This class will examine the prevalence of mental health challenges in elite sport, prevention mechanisms currently in place, and the role of sport psychology in promoting wellbeing. Conceptual frameworks will be presented to clarify the differences and connections between mental illness, mental health, and mental performance. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05, L06

Week 10: Using Emotions Effectively Sport and high-performance contexts are inherently emotional. A common question posed by performers is how to use emotions effectively to support performance. This class will explore how to help performers develop awareness of their emotional states across different situations, and how to regulate or harness those emotions to optimise performance. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05, L06

Week 11: Mindfulness Mindfulness has become one of the most widely used mental skills in sport, performance, and healthcare, yet it is often misunderstood as simply a relaxation technique. This highly applied class will introduce mindfulness as a way of cultivating present-moment awareness, attentional control, and psychological flexibility under pressure. Students will experience a range of individual and group mindfulness exercises while reflecting on how mindfulness can be integrated into various group environments. The class will focus on a case study from professional acting, illustrating how ensemble mindfulness practices can strengthen presence, wellbeing, and performance. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05, L06

Week 12: Adaptive Performance: Perception, Decision Making, and Creativity At the highest levels of performance, success depends not only on making good decisions but also on recognising and creating new possibilities for action. This class will examine how perceptual-cognitive skills and creativity work together to support adaptive performance in dynamic environments. Students will explore evidence-based approaches to developing anticipation, decision-making, attention, and creativity, while critically evaluating emerging technologies such as eye-tracking and virtual reality. Through practical activities and case studies, students will consider how practitioners can design learning environments that enhance both perceptual attunement and creative adaptability. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05, L06
Week 13: Structured Team Debate (Assessment Task) See assessment for details. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05, L06, L07
